about: Every raised and lowered form Unicode has of a digit, a Latin letter, + - = and the round brackets (its <super> and <sub> compatibility forms), with the character it raises or lowers. The server's table (apps/api/app/services/glyphs.py, read by services/script_runs.py for every maths and physics reader and the parser) and the phone's (apps/mobile/lib/unicodeSupSub.ts) are each held to this file, so 'eˣ' reads as e^x on both. not_scripts are characters Unicode also calls superscripts that no reader takes for one, with why. The server test (app/tests/services/test_script_runs.py) also checks this list is Unicode's whole class.

not_scripts.º: masculine ordinal indicator (nº, 1º), and a degree typed in the degree sign's place (30º)
